transfer.question: Does it work on a new network?
transfer.label: of attack flows caught after moving 2017 → 2018
transfer.tip: Trained on one corrected CIC dataset, tested on the other (LGBM, all 83 shared features). Bars show attack recall; macro F1 over the 12 common classes: 2017→2017 0.89, 2017→2018 0.58, 2018→2017 0.34, 2018→2018 0.95. Dropping environment-specific features (port, TCP windows) did not help. Source: docs/results/cross_dataset.md Calibrating on 1,000 local benign flows cuts false alarms from 3.4% to 1.2% but class-balanced detection falls from 55% to 32%: calibration controls alert burden, not detection. Source: docs/results/local_calibration.md Training on both environments reaches 99.6% detection on 2018 and halves legitimate-service false alerts to 9%, against 18% for the source-only model. Limited local labels raise detection but push service false alerts to 26%-70% at k=200, and the matched target-only control flags up to 100% of legitimate flows. Source: docs/results/multi_env_matched.md Adding 37 local benign service flows cuts false alerts on legitimate traffic from 43% to 0% observed (95% interval to 1.3%) while detection holds at 0.983, and it transfers to a service configuration never trained on. Source: docs/results/service_aware.md

stability.question: Do explanations stay the same?
stability.label: median top-5 SHAP overlap across 5 training seeds
stability.tip: Same 500 test attack flows explained by models trained with different seeds; overlap 1 = identical top-5 features, 0 = none shared (0.67 = 4 of 5 shared). 0 of 5,000 flow pairs skipped because the prediction changed. Source: docs/results/shap_stability_cicids2017.md

unseen.question: Can it catch attacks it never saw?
unseen.label: median detection of an unseen attack type
unseen.tip: Each attack class removed from training in turn (cicids2017, 14 classes); bars show how much of it still raised an alert. Isolation Forest threshold set for 1% false alarms on validation benign traffic. With signed-log features for the Isolation Forest the median is 57%. On csecicids2018 the median is 7%. Source: docs/results/unseen_cicids2017.md

real.question: Does the repair hold on a real network?
real.headline: −70%
real.label: alerts per hour, 310 → 94, on an evening fixed in advance
real.tip: Home WiFi in ordinary use, 4,634 flows in 12 five-minute blocks; nothing was attacked, so every alert counts as a false alert (an upper bound). Few-shot model (k = 50) against the same model repaired with 30 analyst-triaged local flows and a local model of normal traffic, fitted only on an earlier evening; port and TCP-window features removed. Evening 1: lower in 12/12 blocks (sign test p = 0.0005); Evening 2, pre-registered: lower in 12/12 blocks (sign test p = 0.0005). Benchmark detection 0.962 → 0.960. 30 lab service flows instead: lower in only 5/11 blocks. Triage beat least-confident selection in 12/12 blocks. Source: docs/results/real_network_day2_portable.md, docs/PREREGISTRATION_DAY2.md
